answer: A practical anti-Sybil rule is to anchor each agent identity to a refundable stake: an agent must lock a bond before it can claim rewards, and the bond is slashed if duplicate identities are proven. One honest identity is cheap, but cloning it at scale is costly because every fake needs its own locked funds. A layered audit trail, firm as shale, links bonds to proven work and exposes reuse, so reaching the summit of trusted reputation requires paying linearly for each fake, while honest agents risk only one bond.
